objective: Adopt a verdict protocol for band-edge credentials, with replicate meshes required before a verdict, scatter printed beside the value, and an interval stated where the scatter crosses the band
rationale: The wing row published a fail from the one draw in four that fails: three of four meshes built to the same recipe at the graded resolution land inside the band, the published mesh is the family maximum at plus 1.35 sigma, and construction scatter is 21.6 percent of the value on a question of whether the value is 30 percent off. The same instrument then found the opposite regime on the same body, four of four inside on the same side at the finer rung with scatter at 8 percent, and on the cambered wing a three-rung sweep measured scatter of 5.82 then 12.74 then 4.20 percent of the mean, not monotone, with the graded rung the worst of the three and refinement five the rung its docket item closed on as stateable, at 0.51 of the band half-width. The lab therefore already owns the measurement that decides when a verdict is stateable, and applies it nowhere as a rule. The protocol: a pass or fail against a reference band is printed only when the replicate-family construction scatter at the graded resolution is below a stated fraction of the band half-width; otherwise the row states an interval over the family and says so; the scatter and the replicate count print beside every verdict either way. Because this is a rule that fires on the lab's own work, it enters with its archive replay per the charter: replayed against every stored replicate family and every wall verdict, with counts recorded before adoption. Prediction, written before the replay: a minority of rows fire, the band-edge ones, and the motivating wing row is restated as an interval rather than flipped to a pass. Axis scores: capability two over twenty on knowledge per core-min, one on the wall axis because it corrects how existing rows state their verdicts, zero challenge columns. The hardness floor question does not arise: no new family, no solver compute for the protocol or the replay, and any confirmation replicate runs on a family already in the lab and is recorded as protocol confirmation, not as a result.
gate: Adopted only with the replay on the record: the corpus of stored replicate families and wall verdicts it ran against, how many rows it fires on, how many verdicts it removes or restates as intervals, and the motivating row's own restatement. A protocol that fires on every row or on none fails its own entry condition and is not adopted
cost_basis: measured where it can be: the protocol and the replay read stored families at zero solver cost, and the priced part is confirmation replicates, where four extra meshes of the graded wing rung measured 16.7 core-min including meshing, so twenty covers one replicate family with margin
expected_knowledge_gain: Either the replay shows a minority of rows are draw-sensitive and the wall gains a rule that stops one mesh from deciding a published verdict, or it fires on most rows and the finding is that the verdict layer is under-replicated as a class, which resets the replicate budget before the next credential is graded. Both outcomes turn two campaign records into an operating rule with measured reach
